children: Pratt & Whitney named Amy Comer president of its Military Engines business, effective Jan. 1, as part of a broader leadership transition at the aerospace and defense company.
Comer will succeed Jill Albertelli, who was recently named president of Pratt & Whitney. Albertelli is taking over from Shane Eddy, who plans to retire at the end of 2026.

Comer has more than 20 years of experience in engineering and program management across military and commercial engine programs. She currently serves as vice president of Pratt & Whitney’s geared turbofan, or GTF, engines business.

For RTX investors, the appointment puts an executive with experience in both engineering and program execution in charge of a military engine portfolio that includes propulsion for the F-35 fighter. The leadership change comes as Pratt & Whitney works to support existing military fleets while developing and upgrading propulsion systems for U.S. and allied defense customers.
Eddy cited Comer’s technical background and execution experience in announcing the appointment, saying she would build on Albertelli’s work in the military engines unit.
Pratt & Whitney is one of RTX’s three main business segments. RTX, which also owns Collins Aerospace and Raytheon, reported more than $88 billion in sales in 2025.

title: RTX names Amy Comer to lead Pratt & Whitney Military Engines
